questions.stem: What is the key difference between addition and condensation polymerisation?

options.text: Addition uses heat but condensation does not
Condensation releases a small molecule (usually water) as a by-product, while addition does not
Addition polymers are stronger than condensation polymers
Condensation only uses one type of monomer

questions.explanation: In condensation polymerisation, a small molecule (usually water) is released each time two monomers join. In addition polymerisation, the C=C double bond simply opens up and monomers join with no other product formed. Condensation also typically requires two different types of monomers.

questions.stem: What type of link is formed in a polyamide such as nylon?
questions.explanation: Polyamides like nylon contain amide links (-CONH-). These form when the -COOH group of a dicarboxylic acid reacts with the -NH2 group of a diamine, releasing water. The amide link is also called a peptide bond when found in proteins.
